cohort: 138,910 newborns, 13,206 delivered by elective cesarean and 125,704 delivered vaginally, singleton, uncomplicated deliveries and pregnancies between 1991 and 2014
finding: Children delivered by elective cesarean section are at an increased risk for hospitalization with pediatric infectious morbidity compared with vaginally delivered children.
mod_finding: Children delivered by elective cesarean section are at an increased risk for hospitalization with pediatric infectious morbidity compared with vaginally delivered children.
